chunks: And in the narration of Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, from him, peace be upon him, he said:

"Every act of injustice by which a man wrongs himself in Makkah, whether theft, wronging someone, or any kind of wrongdoing, I indeed regard it as ilḥād. And for that reason, the jurists used to avoid residing in Makkah."

key_terms.إِلْحَاداً: deviation or profanation in the sacred precinct by committing wrongdoing
key_terms.الْفُقَهَاءُ: the jurists or learned scholars of fiqh
key_terms.سَرِقَةٍ: theft as a specific form of wrongdoing
key_terms.ظُلْمٍ: injustice or wrongdoing in a general sense

ai.seo_question: Why did the jurists avoid residing in Makkah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that wrongdoing committed in Makkah carries a grave moral character, such that the Imam عليه السلام describes it as ilḥād. It also indicates the caution of the fuqahāʾ, who avoided living there out of fear of falling into sin in a sacred sanctuary.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2330 - In a narration from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, from him (Imam Abu Abdullah (as)):

"Every act of injustice a person commits against himself in Mecca—be it theft, oppression of someone, or any form of wrongdoing—I consider it to be deviation (ilhad). For this reason, the jurists avoided residing in Mecca."
